Cyber Attack Disrupts Spanish Hospitality Sector, Hotel Chains Hit by Ransomware

Madrid, June 17 – A large-scale cyber attack targeting the Spanish hospitality industry has forced several hotel and restaurant chains to shut down booking systems and suspend online services, disrupting operations for staff and guests across the country, industry officials said Monday.

The incident, which began late Sunday, appears to involve a ransomware attack on the IT networks of major hospitality firms, including leading hotel operators such as Hotelia Iberica and SolMar Resorts, as well as restaurant group Casa del Sabor. The attackers are believed to have encrypted key data, demanding payment to restore access, according to people familiar with the matter.

Hotelia Iberica said in a statement that it had “temporarily disabled digital check-in and reservation platforms as a precaution,” and was assisting guests manually at reception desks. “We are doing everything possible to minimize inconvenience to our guests and to support our staff in affected locations,” the company added, without specifying the number of sites hit.

Employees at SolMar Resorts reported difficulties accessing shift schedules, payroll information and guest records. “We started our shift and suddenly the computers wouldn’t work. All bookings had to be checked by phone or in person,” said Lucía Fernández, a front desk supervisor at a SolMar property in Valencia.

The attack has also impacted restaurant operations. Casa del Sabor, which operates over 200 outlets nationwide, confirmed that its point-of-sale systems were offline at numerous sites. “Our teams are reverting to manual order taking and cash transactions where possible,” said managing director Jorge Ruiz. “We are working closely with cybersecurity experts to resolve the situation.”

The National Hospitality Association of Spain called the incident “the most serious cyber attack to date on our sector,” estimating that more than 500 hotels and restaurants had already been affected. “The immediate impact is significant, with many staff unable to perform their normal duties and guests experiencing delays and disruptions,” said association president Marta Gómez.

Spanish law enforcement agencies have launched an investigation, but officials say the attack is ongoing and recovery efforts may take several days. At affected properties, workers are supporting guests with check-ins, check-outs and meal orders using paper records and manual processes.

“We ask for patience and understanding from all guests and staff as we restore normal operations,” Gómez said. “The hospitality sector is resilient and our priority is to ensure safety and service even under these challenging circumstances.”
